title: Petra and the Provision
premise: Elodie Ashgrove, captain of the riverboat Provision, dredges up a sealed chest bearing the crest of Vessia, a drowned kingdom whose heirs were supposedly exterminated. Inside are letters naming Elodie's late mother as the last legitimate claimant—making Elodie an heir to a throne everyone powerful wants never to exist. Hunted by the Chancellery's agents and shadowed by Wren, a charming archivist who may be spy or ally or both, Elodie must run the river upstream to the forbidden source where proof of legitimacy—and the truth of her mother's betrayal of Vessia—waits in a flooded archive. At the source, Elodie chooses to burn the inheritance rather than wield it, breaking the cycle of power that killed her mother, and returns downstream to a life chosen freely, with Wren at their side.
about_author: Odile Underhill spent seven years working seasonal freight on inland waterways before turning to writing full-time. She lives in a converted lockkeeper's cottage and claims she can still read a river's mood from the smell of the morning air.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A routine salvage run snags on something heavy: a lead-lined chest stamped with Vessia's seal. Elodie nearly dumps it back into the current, but greed—or curiosity—wins. The beat is uneasy temptation; the river has offered a gift that feels like a debt.

chapters.title: The Dead Nation's Postage
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with a letter fragment in Wren's voice as interlude. Prying the chest open reveals correspondence proving Elodie's mother was Vessia's hidden heir. Elodie burns one letter and keeps the rest—a compromise that will cost them. Beat: dread disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren boards at Corvane Landing posing as a surveyor for the Chancellery, tasked with recovering the chest. Watching Elodie work the boat, Wren begins to doubt the mission. Beat: attraction sharpened by deception; duty starts to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Chancellery Men
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Agents board at a toll lock demanding inspection. Elodie lies smoothly, but they leave a tracker aboard. That night Elodie finds it, and realizes someone aboard let them past the first checkpoint. Beat: paranoia; trust becomes cargo that might be counterfeit.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Weir
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren catches Elodie preparing to abandon ship; Elodie catches Wren transmitting a report. Guns come out, then honesty: Wren confesses everything and offers to feed the Chancellery false coordinates. Beat: love declared against duty, fragile as wet paper.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Together they run the narrowing gorge above the last charted mile, dodging patrols and the dry season's falling waterline. An old pilot's journal hints the source archive floods open only at high snowmelt—days away. Beat: partnership forged under pressure; hope rationed like fuel.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In a river-town of Vessian exiles, Elodie learns her mother didn't flee the purge—she traded the archive's location for Elodie's life. Grief curdles into fury: the inheritance is built on a bargain Elodie never consented to. Beat: the theme of inheritance turns poisonous.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Chancellery gunboat corners them in a shrinking channel; Wren offers themselves as bait so the Provision can slip through the shallows. Elodie refuses to sacrifice them, and they barely escape together as the river drops below safe depth. Beat: love against duty resolved in action, not words.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the forbidden spring, the flooded archive stands open in the last hours of snowmelt. Elodie reads the full record of Vessia's corruption—kings who poisoned rivals, ministers who starved provinces—and understands why her mother hid. Beat: climax of understanding; power revealed as the true villain.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing with Wren. Elodie feeds the archive to the spring and lets the current carry the ash downstream, ending the claim forever. They turn the boat around, running home with the dry season wind at their backs. Beat: release—the river gives nothing back, and that is finally enough.
